title: Quickstart templates: Catalog & support matrix (v1)
author: Wei Chen
related_pages: Template secrets and local dev policy
body:
## Purpose
This page defines the **template catalog and support matrix** for Redwood Inference “Quickstart templates (RAG + agents)” v1. It is intended to be a single, stable reference for:
- Which templates we ship and their **support tier**
- Supported **languages/runtimes** and required versions
- Supported **backends** (with default choices and extension points)
- Per-template **maintenance SLA** expectations (bug/security fixes, deprecations, and compatibility windows)

This is a living document; changes should be accompanied by an update to the docs site landing pages and the compatibility matrix in `redwood-quickstarts`.

---

## Definitions
- **Template**: An opinionated reference implementation in `redwood-quickstarts` designed to be run locally in <15 minutes and deployed in <60 minutes.
- **Supported backend**: A backend for which we provide working code, configuration docs, and CI coverage (at minimum, a smoke test).
- **Extension backend**: A backend we document as an example integration pattern, but do not continuously test in CI.
- **Support tier**: Our commitment level for fixes, updates, and operational guidance (see “Maintenance SLA”).

---

## Template catalog (v1)
The following templates constitute v1.

| Template name | Repo path (redwood-quickstarts) | Primary language | Framework | Use case | Status | Support tier |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| RAG Service (API) + Ingestion Worker (Python) | `templates/rag/python-fastapi` | Python | FastAPI + background worker | Document ingestion + retrieval + answer generation | GA | Tier 1 |
| RAG Service (TypeScript) | `templates/rag/typescript-node` | TypeScript | Node (Express) | RAG API with streaming + request correlation | GA | Tier 1 |
| Agents Service (Python) | `templates/agents/python-fastapi` | Python | FastAPI | Tool-calling agent patterns (allow-lists, timeouts, schema validation) | GA | Tier 1 |
| Agents Service (TypeScript) | `templates/agents/typescript-node` | TypeScript | Node (Express) | Tool-calling agent patterns with streaming and proxy-safe settings | Beta | Tier 2 |
| RAG + Agent (Python) | `templates/rag-agent/python-fastapi` | Python | FastAPI | Planner/executor with retrieval as a tool; prompt injection guardrails | GA | Tier 1 |
| RAG + Agent (TypeScript) | `templates/rag-agent/typescript-node` | TypeScript | Node (Express) | Combined flow with retrieval tool + structured output | Beta | Tier 2 |
| (Experimental) Minimal RAG (Go) | `experimental/rag/go-http` | Go | net/http | Advisor sample for teams standardizing on Go | Experimental | Tier 3 |

Notes:
- “GA” means we expect production use with normal hardening and customer-specific security review.
- “Beta” means functionality is solid, but we expect some API ergonomics and edge-case fixes post-launch.
- “Experimental” is not recommended for production use; it is guidance only.

---

## Feature support matrix
This matrix captures what each template includes by default.

| Capability | Python RAG | TS RAG | Python Agents | TS Agents | Python RAG+Agent | TS RAG+Agent |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Redwood Hosted API integration (chat/generate) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Streaming responses | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Request ID + correlation ID propagation | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| OpenTelemetry traces (server + client) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Metrics: latency, token usage, error class | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Structured logs (JSON) w/ redaction guidance | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Retries/backoff + timeout defaults | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| 429 handling guidance (respect Retry-After) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Health endpoints + graceful shutdown | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Docker Compose dev stack | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Minimal Kubernetes manifests | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Tool calling allow-list + per-tool timeout wrapper | N/A | N/A | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Tool output schema validation (JSON schema) | N/A | N/A | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Prompt injection & tool misuse guardrails | Yes (RAG-focused) | Yes (RAG-focused) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Eval harness hook (quickstart-compatible runner) | Partial (documented) | Partial (documented) | Partial (documented) | Partial (documented) | Yes | Yes |

Legend:
- “Partial” typically means we provide a working configuration + docs, but do not run it in CI on every PR.

---

## Backend support (v1)
### Vector store / retrieval backends
We intentionally support a small set out of the gate.

| Backend | Classification | Default for templates | Where used | CI coverage | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| Qdrant (Docker) | Supported backend | Yes | Python RAG, TS RAG, Python RAG+Agent, TS RAG+Agent | Yes | Default local dev path via Docker Compose. Low-friction for onboarding.
| Postgres + pgvector | Supported backend | Optional | Python RAG, Python RAG+Agent | Partial | Supported as a documented alternative; recommended for teams already operating Postgres.
| Pinecone | Extension backend | No | RAG templates (adapter example) | No | Example integration pattern only; not tested continuously.

### Document ingestion sources
| Source type | Classification | Included by default | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Local files (PDF/TXT/MD) | Supported | Yes | Provided loader + chunking defaults with guidance on PII and secrets.
| S3 / cloud object storage | Extension | No | Documented pattern only; customer-specific security considerations.
| Web crawl | Not supported | No | Out of scope for v1 (avoid unsafe crawling defaults).

### Agent tool backends
| Tool type | Classification | Included by default | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| HTTP tools (internal services) | Supported | Yes | Allow-list required; per-tool timeout and error handling required.
| “Retriever” as a tool | Supported | Yes (in RAG+Agent) | Retrieval invoked through tool calling; designed to be auditable.
| SQL/database tools | Extension | No | Documented pattern; must include query allow-list and read-only credentials.
| Browser automation | Not supported | No | Explicitly excluded due to safety risk and operational complexity.

---

## Language/runtime support policy
We keep runtimes intentionally narrow to reduce drift and ticket volume.

| Language | Supported versions | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Python | 3.10–3.12 | CI covers 3.11 by default; templates should run on 3.10+.
| Node.js / TypeScript | Node 18 LTS / 20 LTS | CI covers Node 20 by default; ensure fetch/streaming behavior is proxy-safe.
| Go | 1.22+ (experimental) | Only for the experimental template; no GA commitment.

Dependency policy:
- Templates may pin dependencies more aggressively than product SDKs to avoid onboarding breakages.
- Security patches may trigger patch releases even when no template code changes are required.

---

## Maintenance SLA (by support tier)
This SLA describes how DevEx and the template owners handle issues discovered internally, via CI, or via Support tickets.

### Tier 1 (Active / GA)
Applies to: Python RAG, TS RAG, Python Agents, Python RAG+Agent
- **Bug fixes**: triage within **2 business days**, patch release target within **10 business days** for high-impact onboarding bugs.
- **Security fixes**: acknowledge within **1 business day**; patch timeline driven by severity:
  - Critical: fix/release within **72 hours**
  - High: **7 days**
  - Medium/Low: **30 days** or next scheduled maintenance release
- **Compatibility window**: support latest **2 minor** versions of `redwood-sdk-*` used by templates, plus a 30-day overlap period.
- **CI**: required smoke test coverage against staging, including telemetry emission checks.
- **Docs freshness**: docs snippets must be auto-verified or updated within **1 release cycle** if drift is detected.

### Tier 2 (Beta)
Applies to: TS Agents, TS RAG+Agent
- **Bug fixes**: triage within **5 business days**; patch release target **best effort**.
- **Security fixes**: same severity timelines as Tier 1 for critical/high; medium/low best effort.
- **CI**: smoke tests required, but may be narrower in coverage (e.g., subset of scenarios).
- **Known issues**: must be documented on the “Quickstart template known issues” page within **5 business days** of confirmation.

### Tier 3 (Experimental)
Applies to: Go minimal RAG
- **No SLA** on fixes. Updates may occur opportunistically.
- **No CI requirement**.
- Must include prominent “experimental” labeling and link to Tier 1 templates for production guidance.

---

## Template ownership and escalation
Primary ownership is DevEx; escalation paths route through Support and SRE when operational guardrails are involved.

| Area | DRI (primary) | Backup | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Python templates | Sabrina James | Wei Chen | Owns runtime behavior, config defaults, and docs in repo.
| TypeScript templates | Dana Lo | Monica Patel | Owns Node streaming behavior and error handling examples.
| SDK helper defaults (retry/timeout/streaming) | Monica Patel | Ibrahim Khan | Changes require SRE review for safe defaults.
| Telemetry contract and validations | Allison Grant | Logan Wright | Must align with Console dashboards and cardinality guidelines.
| Observability pack (dashboards/alerts) | Sergio Costa | Aisha Bello | Owns thresholds and anti-noise rules.
| Security guidance / secrets handling | Naomi Feldman | Marcus Lin | Reviews logging and PII guidance; approves local dev patterns.

Escalation triggers:
- P0 onboarding breakage (templates fail to run) → DevEx + SDK lead + on-call SRE (if infra-related)
- Telemetry regression (missing required attributes/metrics) → Telemetry standards + DevEx
- Reports of unsafe tool patterns or PII leakage risk → Security review within 1 business day

---

## Support boundaries (what we will/won’t help with)
We will support:
- Running templates locally using documented prerequisites
- Deploying via provided Docker Compose/Kubernetes manifests (as a starting point)
- Troubleshooting Redwood API/SDK configuration, retries/timeouts, and 429 behavior
- Telemetry setup and verification in Redwood Console (request correlation, token/cost attribution)

We will not support (v1):
- Arbitrary vector DBs not listed above as supported/extension backends
- Full agent framework customization (planner design, long-horizon memory, multi-agent runtimes)
- Web crawling or browser automation tooling
- Customer-specific compliance sign-off (we provide patterns; customers must validate policies)

---

## Adding a new backend or template (process)
1. Propose in DevEx Slack with: use case, expected audience, security considerations, and operational risk.
2. Provide a minimal adapter interface and a runnable local example.
3. Define CI coverage expectations (smoke test at minimum for “Supported backend”).
4. Security review for secrets/PII and tool-safety (if agent-related).
5. Update this matrix + docs-site landing page before release.

---

## Dedicated / Private considerations (support stance)
All Tier 1 templates should provide a clear path to:
- **Dedicated**: configure routing policies, capacity expectations, and timeout guidance under sustained throughput
- **Private (VPC/on-prem)**: note networking constraints (egress, DNS), secrets management integration points (KMS/HSM), and audit logging expectations

We do not guarantee that the provided Kubernetes manifests are production-ready for every Private deployment, but they should be a correct starting point and follow safe defaults.

---

## Change log
- 2026-02-18: Marked Python templates GA Tier 1; set TS Agents and TS RAG+Agent to Beta Tier 2; clarified backend classifications (supported vs extension).
